end.summary:
Practised that the sum of the first n odd numbers is n².
Saanvi correctly gave 1–5 odd-number sum = 25 and 1–29 sum = 225.
Used two joined triangles to explain 10 + 15 = 25 as a 5×5 dot square.
Initially said odd-number addition always gives an odd number; this was not corrected by the end.
Teach-back was not passed; the new-case picture explanation remained incomplete.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the pattern that adding the first n odd numbers makes n², using dot rows and two joined triangles. Saanvi successfully explained how 10 and 15 form five rows of five dots and correctly found 225 for the odd numbers from 1 to 29. One mix-up remained: they treated every sum of odd numbers as odd, and this was not corrected later. At home, ask Saanvi to draw the 5×5 dot square from the 10-dot and 15-dot triangles and label each row.
